product.name: KeePassXC
product.idguide: NOT FOUND in the public documentation read on 8 November 2026.
product.additional:
Illustrative example for the Cyber Manual Movement, built by the Value Chain Risk Institute with the CRA Manual Builder from public documentation read on 8 November 2026. It is NOT the manufacturer's manual and makes no claim about CRA conformity. Gaps are marked NOT FOUND rather than filled in.
Desktop password manager for Windows, macOS and Linux, licensed GPL v3. Password managers are listed in CRA Annex III, Class I. KeePassXC is developed by a volunteer team, and its Windows installer names DroidMonkey Apps, LLC as publisher. Whether anyone is a CRA manufacturer here, or the non-commercial and open-source steward provisions apply, is left to the working group.

er1.2b: Browser integration, Secret Service, SSH agent and network features are off until the user enables them. Quick Unlock (Windows Hello, Touch ID) is ON by default on Windows and macOS and can be disabled under Application Settings > Security.
er1.2g:
The product only processes the following data:
Credentials, notes and attachments the user stores
Favicons, only if the user enables downloading them

er2.v-test: Independent reviews: ANSSI Security Visa ANSSI-CSPN-2025/16 (17 November 2025, valid to 17 November 2028, version 2.7.9 on Windows 10) and an application security review by Zaur Molotnikov (19 January 2023, version 2.7.4). Reports are published at keepassxc.org/audits.
er2.v-sbom: NOT FOUND in the public documentation read on 8 November 2026.
er2.v-pub: NOT FOUND in the public documentation read on 8 November 2026.
er2.v-cvd: SECURITY.md: report privately through a GitHub Security Advisory, private Matrix messages to named team members, or email. No public channels for first reports. Reporters should not go to a CVE Numbering Authority before the team confirms, unless the team has not responded within 30 days.
er2.v-dist: Packages are signed and published with SHA-256 digests; see chapter 3.4.

sp.title: Database encryption
sp.desc: The database is encrypted with AES-256 or Twofish and is encrypted at all times on disk.

sp.title: Key derivation against guessing
sp.desc: With KDBX 4, the Argon2 key derivation function (recommended) transforms the composite master key, making dictionary attacks slower.

sp.title: Additional unlock factors
sp.desc: A key file and hardware-key challenge-response (YubiKey, OnlyKey) can be added to the master password.

sp.title: Protected attributes
sp.desc: Attributes marked Protect are hidden by default and shown only on Reveal.

sp.title: No network access by default
sp.desc: Network access is opt-in (favicon downloads); a build without networking code is possible.

sp.title: Signed releases
sp.desc: Every package ships with a PGP signature and a SHA-256 digest. The Windows MSI carries an Authenticode signature (DroidMonkey Apps, LLC); macOS builds are signed with the project's Apple Developer ID and checked at launch.

cc.title: Host computer and operating system
cc.desc: The Windows, macOS or Linux computer KeePassXC runs on.

cc.title: Database storage location
cc.desc: Local disk, a synced folder or a remote location holding the database file.

cc.title: Web browser with KeePassXC-Browser
cc.desc: A browser with the extension installed from its official store.

cc.title: Hardware key
cc.desc: A YubiKey or OnlyKey configured for challenge-response.

cc.title: Distribution channels
cc.desc: keepassxc.org, Microsoft Store, winget, Chocolatey, Homebrew, Flathub, Snap and distribution packages.

cc.title: Other applications
cc.desc: Programs that receive Auto-Type keystrokes or Secret Service and SSH agent requests.

cp.title: User
cp.desc: The person who keeps passwords in the database.

cp.title: Administrator
cp.desc: A person enforcing settings through Windows Group Policy.

cz.title: User's computer
cz.desc: The host computer and its user account

cz.title: Storage and sync services
cz.desc: Places outside the computer where the database is stored or synced

fc.title: Store and retrieve credentials
fc.desc: Create, edit, search and copy entries in an encrypted KDBX database.
fc.rfu: Keeping the only copy of the database on one device.

fc.title: Fill credentials in the browser
fc.desc: Browser integration with KeePassXC-Browser, including passkeys.

fc.title: Auto-Type into other applications
fc.desc: Type the username and password into the previously selected window.

fc.title: Unlock the database
fc.desc: Unlock with the master password and optional key file or hardware key, or with Quick Unlock (biometrics).
fc.rfu: Quick Unlock on a computer account other people use.

fc.title: Share and sync databases
fc.desc: KeeShare shared groups and remote database synchronisation.

fc.title: Install security updates
fc.desc: Install the newest signed release from the channel used for installation.

cu.title: Strong master password
cu.desc: Use a strong master password; add a key file or hardware key for more protection.

cu.title: Keep backups
cu.desc: Back up the database, key files and hardware-key secrets (the user guide explains creating a YubiKey backup).

cu.affected: CC01 Host computer and operating system
cu.title: Use a computer you trust
cu.desc: Run KeePassXC only on a computer that is kept updated and free of malware.

cu.title: Official extension only
cu.desc: Install KeePassXC-Browser only from the official browser stores and connect only your own browsers.

cu.title: Check the target window
cu.desc: Before Auto-Type, make sure the intended window has focus.

cu.title: Quick Unlock only on a personal account
cu.desc: Disable Quick Unlock if other people can use the same computer account or biometrics.

cu.title: Trusted storage and sharing
cu.desc: Store or sync the database only in locations you control or trust, and share groups only with intended people.

cu.title: Official, verified downloads
cu.desc: Install from keepassxc.org or an official channel. On Windows, check that the verified publisher is DroidMonkey Apps, LLC; for other sources, verify the PGP signature.

ri.title: Weak master password
ri.desc: A short or reused master password without another factor.
ri.risk: Anyone who obtains the database file can guess the password offline.

ri.title: No backup
ri.desc: The only copy of the database, key file or hardware-key secret is lost.

ri.title: Compromised computer
ri.desc: Malware runs on the host computer.
ri.risk: Credentials can be captured while the database is unlocked.

ri.title: Unofficial browser extension
ri.desc: An extension from another source is connected.
ri.risk: Credentials are handed to an attacker-controlled extension.

ri.title: Auto-Type into the wrong window
ri.desc: The focused window is not the intended one.
ri.risk: The password is typed into a chat, a document or a hostile page.

ri.title: Quick Unlock on a shared account
ri.desc: Quick Unlock stays enabled on a computer account others use.
ri.risk: Another person can unlock the database.

ri.title: Untrusted storage or sharing
ri.desc: The database is kept or shared in a location others control.
ri.risk: The encrypted file is exposed to offline attack or tampering.

ri.title: Tampered installer
ri.desc: KeePassXC is installed from an unofficial source without verification.
ri.risk: A modified program can steal every credential.

commissioning:
Download from keepassxc.org or an official channel and verify it (chapter 3.4).
Create a database in KDBX 4 format with Argon2.
Set a strong master password; optionally add a key file or hardware key.
Decide whether Quick Unlock should stay enabled.
Set up a backup of the database.

updates.note: Install new releases from the channel used for installation. Flatpak (recommended on Linux) and store channels can update automatically; website downloads are replaced with the new signed package. Verify signatures as described at keepassxc.org/verifying-signatures.
updates.disableAuto: No in-app update mechanism was found in the documentation read; automatic updating depends on the distribution channel.
updates.end: NOT FOUND: no support period is published.

decommission:
Delete the database files, key files and backups from every location they were stored.
Remove the browser extension, then uninstall KeePassXC.
